comparison: Both strongly support the finding that endogenous DVL2 forms large complexes (C1-C6, C65). OpenEval notes converging evidence from multiple assays with some uncertainty about size estimation assumptions. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as a strength, stating 'endogenous DVL2 forms large complexes in a higher proportion as DVL1/3.'

Both address functional validation in DVL knockout cells (C97-C106). OpenEval finds the evidence strongly supportive with comprehensive validation. Peer reviewers acknowledge improvements with tKO cells but express uncertainty, stating the manuscript 'does not address the requirements of DVL2 condensation for WNT signalling' at truly endogenous levels, considering the experiments useful but insufficient.

Both address CFR identification and characterization (C17-C22, C31, C39). OpenEval finds strong support through systematic deletion/fusion experiments. Peer reviewers acknowledge the identification but express uncertainty, noting 'several of the described effects are partial...often indicating that the targeted domains contribute, but are not required,' suggesting contribution rather than absolute requirement.

Both evaluate structure-guided mutagenesis and CFR mechanism (C41-C48, C53). OpenEval finds strong support from convergent deletion, mutation, and co-localization data. Peer reviewers acknowledge characterization in overexpression systems but express uncertainty about requirements at endogenous levels, noting partial effects.

Both address DVL2 paralog specificity (C7, C88-C91). OpenEval finds strong support for DVL2-specific CFR-mediated complex formation through multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly accept this finding, noting 'DVL2 forms large complexes in a higher proportion as DVL1/3' and finding the DVL1 rewiring experiments 'quite interesting.'

Both address CFR transplantation to DVL1 (C34, C38, plus C32-C33, C35-C37 in peer). OpenEval finds strong support that CFR is sufficient to confer complex-forming ability. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this, stating the manuscript 'shows that one of those motifs (CFR) rewires o/e DVL1 into behaving similarly as DVL2.'

Both address phase separation characterization (C55-C59, C62-C64). OpenEval finds support through standard biophysical perturbations but notes these methods are not entirely specific. Peer reviewers do not explicitly critique these experiments, with the editor noting 'functional validation of the DVL2 intrinsically disordered regions' as a contribution, implicitly accepting the characterization.

Both address the hierarchical assembly model (C66-C67, C70-C72, C73, C111). OpenEval finds the model plausible but uncertain, noting data don't directly demonstrate sequential assembly and alternative explanations aren't excluded. Peer reviewers don't explicitly evaluate this model but express uncertainty about whether overexpression-derived models reflect endogenous behavior.

Both address C-terminal region importance and correlation with function (C12-C15, C32-C33 in OpenEval; C13-C16 in peer). OpenEval finds strong support for functional relationships. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about interpreting correlations as requirements, noting 'partial effects...indicating that the targeted domains contribute, but are not required.'

Both address CFR sufficiency through gain-of-function experiments (C23-C26, C29-C30). OpenEval finds support that CFR cooperates with polymerization domains. Peer reviewers don't explicitly critique these DIX domain requirement and localization findings, treating them as supporting observations.

Both address nuclear localization as a potential confound (C27-C28). OpenEval finds this control strengthens conclusions by showing similar differences in cytosolic condensates. Peer reviewers don't explicitly critique these findings, accepting them as supporting observations.

Both address phase separation through functional replacement experiments (C62-C64). OpenEval finds strong support that phase-separating activity rather than specific sequence is crucial. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the 'functional validation of the DVL2 intrinsically disordered regions' without explicit critique.

Both address functional differences between LCR4 and CD2 (C35-C37, C68-C69 in OpenEval; C35-C38 in peer). OpenEval finds support for a two-step assembly model. Peer reviewers acknowledge the CFR rewiring experiments that include these observations.

Both address paralog differences and functional models (C49, C92-C96 in OpenEval; C92-C96 in peer). OpenEval finds experimental data supported but mechanistic explanations speculative. Peer reviewers accept the paralog-specific behavior as a key finding without explicitly evaluating the 'super scaffold' model.

OpenEval addresses correlation analysis (C107) finding statistical support but noting correlation doesn't establish causation. Peer reviewers address broader functional validation including this correlation, expressing uncertainty about endogenous-level requirements despite acknowledging improvements.

OpenEval addresses dominant-negative effect of isolated CFR (C50-C52) finding support with reasonable but speculative mechanism. Peer reviewers address broader CFR characterization including these observations, acknowledging characterization but expressing uncertainty about absolute requirements.

OpenEval addresses DIX domain role exclusion (C9-C11) finding strong support through multiple converging approaches including M2 mutation testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific aspect.

OpenEval addresses connection to stickers model theoretical framework (C73-C75) finding data consistent but largely speculative. No explicit peer review evaluation of this theoretical interpretation found.

OpenEval identifies multiple explicitly speculative claims (C8, C16, C40, C52, C79, C80, C83, C85, C96) as uncertain, representing hypotheses requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these as speculative claims found.

OpenEval addresses background knowledge and literature review (C112-C138) finding appropriate contextualization and accurate representation of the field. No corresponding peer review evaluation of background claims found.

OpenEval addresses abstract summary claims (C108-C111) finding accurate representation of study findings. Peer reviewers address C111 as part of the hierarchical model evaluation (R7) but don't separately evaluate abstract accuracy.
OpenEval addresses LCR4 and CD2 cooperation (C54) finding reasonable inference from deletion experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing this cooperative model found.

OpenEval addresses citations of prior work on DVL2 conformational regulation (C81, C82, C84) finding accurate representation. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual citations found.

OpenEval addresses citations of prior work on DVL paralog differences (C86, C93, C95) finding appropriate contextualization. Peer reviewers address C93, C95 as part of paralog findings (R8) but don't separately evaluate citation accuracy.
OpenEval addresses established field knowledge (C76) finding well-supported context. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this background claim found.
